title: A Pesar de: Despite the Difficulty

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *a pesar de* + noun or infinitive, *a pesar de que* + clause and *pese a* from B1 Unit 32. They grant a difficulty and go on. The story of settlers in a dry, windy land is full of them.

sections.title: Despite the difficulty
rows: A pesar del frío, los colonos se quedaron.
A pesar de que la tierra era seca, no se fueron.
*a pesar de que* + full clause, indicative for a real fact
A pesar de ser seca, la tierra dio trigo.
Pese a las malas cosechas, no se fueron.

items.spanish: A pesar de las dificultades del clima, los colonos galeses se quedaron.
items.english: Despite the difficulties of the climate, the Welsh settlers stayed.

items.spanish: A pesar de que la tierra era seca, los colonos no se fueron.
items.english: Although the land was dry, the settlers did not leave.

items.spanish: Pese a las malas cosechas, los colonos no se fueron.
items.english: Despite the bad harvests, the settlers did not leave.

items.spanish: A pesar de ser una región fría, la Patagonia recibe muchos visitantes.
items.english: Despite being a cold region, Patagonia receives many visitors.

sections.content: *A pesar de* is followed by a noun or an infinitive; before a full clause you need *a pesar de que*. Do not say *a pesar que el frío*. *Pese a* + noun is the shorter, more formal form.
